# Labour Party Manifesto 2015 Summary: Britain Can Be Better

The 2015 Labour Manifesto presents a vision of national renewal built on the fundamental principle that **Britain only succeeds when working people succeed**. At its core, the document argues that the economy has stopped working for ordinary families, with the historic link between national prosperity and household finances now broken.

## Fiscal Responsibility
Labour commits to a "Budget Responsibility Lock" guaranteeing deficit reduction every year, with national debt falling as soon as possible. Every manifesto commitment is fully funded without additional borrowing—achieved through asking the wealthiest one percent to pay more via a restored 50p tax rate, abolishing non-dom status, and tackling tax avoidance.

## Economy and Work
The manifesto diagnoses a cost-of-living crisis caused by stagnating wages, insecure employment, and markets failing consumers. Labour proposes raising the minimum wage above £8, banning exploitative zero-hours contracts, promoting the Living Wage, and establishing a British Investment Bank to support businesses. Young people would receive guaranteed apprenticeships and reduced tuition fees of £6,000.

## Public Services
The NHS, described as one of Labour's proudest achievements, would receive investment in 20,000 nurses, 8,000 GPs, and 3,000 midwives, funded by a Mansion Tax. Mental health would achieve parity with physical health. Education budgets would be protected, with qualified teachers guaranteed and class sizes capped for young children.

## Families and Communities
Policies include expanded free childcare, doubled paternity leave, 200,000 new homes annually, and abolition of the Bedroom Tax. Immigration would be controlled through stronger borders while preventing exploitation of migrant workers.

## Devolution and Democracy
Labour proposes the biggest devolution in a century through an English Devolution Act, a Constitutional Convention, votes at 16, and replacing the Lords with an elected Senate.

## International Engagement
Britain would remain in a reformed EU, maintain NATO commitment, address climate change as a security priority, and uphold the 0.7% international development commitment.

The manifesto presents a choice: continue with Conservative policies benefiting only the privileged few, or change direction toward shared prosperity where opportunity belongs to everyone.
